title_en: Fable and classical story: how a tale is told
q_en: How does a tale begin, move and end, and who is speaking?
q_ar: كَيْفَ تَبْدَأُ الْحِكَايَةُ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَسِيرُ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَنْتَهِي؟ وَمَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟
not_yet: Every rare word of a classical tale: some are glossed, so read the shape of the tale first.
Whole books of tales, with tales inside tales: here you read one page.
Tales in verse and proverbs: Lesson 93.
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ نَادِرَةٍ فِي الْحِكَايَةِ الْقَدِيمَةِ: بَعْضُهَا مَشْرُوحٌ، فَاقْرَأْ شَكْلَ الْحِكَايَةِ أَوَّلًا.
كُتُبُ الْحِكَايَاتِ كَامِلَةً، وَفِيهَا حِكَايَاتٌ دَاخِلَ حِكَايَاتٍ: هُنَا تَقْرَأُ صَفْحَةً وَاحِدَةً.
الْحِكَايَةُ فِي الشِّعْرِ وَالْأَمْثَالُ: فِي الدَّرْسِ ٩٣.

sents: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ يَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي.
They claimed that a monkey used to live near the wadi.
يُحْكَى أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً سَكَنَتْ تَحْتَ شَجَرَةٍ.
It is told that a tortoise lived under a tree.
وَكَانَ قِرْدٌ شَابٌّ قَدْ سَكَنَ هُنَاكَ.
And a young monkey had settled there.
فَخَرَجَ الْقِرْدُ إِلَى الْوَادِي فَوَجَدَ شَجَرَةً فَصَعِدَ إِلَيْهَا.
So the monkey went out to the wadi, found a tree and climbed it.
فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَأْكُلُ إِذَا سَقَطَتْ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ.
While he was eating, suddenly a fig fell into the water.

lines: What are the first two words of sentences 1 and 2? What do they tell the listener?
مَا الْكَلِمَتَانِ الْأُولَيَانِ فِي الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ ١ وَ٢؟ مَاذَا تَقُولَانِ لِلسَّامِعِ؟
Sentence 4: how many verbs start with فَـ? What do they say about the order of events?
الْجُمْلَةُ ٤: كَمْ فِعْلًا يَبْدَأُ بِـ «فَـ»؟ مَاذَا تَقُولُ عَنْ تَرْتِيبِ الْأَحْدَاثِ؟
Sentence 5: which two words mean “while … suddenly”?

slides.head_ar: لِلْحِكَايَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَجْزَاءٍ: بِدَايَةٌ وَسِلْسِلَةٌ وَمُفَاجَأَةٌ وَعِبْرَةٌ.

cards.def_en: “They claim that …” / “It is told that …”. After أَنَّ the noun ends in ـَ / ـً.
Each فَـ means “and so, next”. Read the chain like a list.
“While … suddenly …”: what follows إِذَا is the surprise.
The tale ends with its lesson: “So this is a lesson for …”.

slides.head_en: A habit and a “had”: كَانَ + present, كَانَ … قَدْ + past
rows: used to live near the wadi
slides.tip: A tale first sets the scene with كَانَ, then moves on with plain past verbs after فَـ.
slides.tip_ar: تَبْدَأُ الْحِكَايَةُ بِـ «كَانَ» لِوَصْفِ الْمَكَانِ، ثُمَّ تَسِيرُ الْأَحْدَاثُ بِأَفْعَالٍ مَاضِيَةٍ بَعْدَ «فَـ».

rows: بَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَمْشِي إِذَا سَمِعَ صَوْتًا
slides.note: Read a فَـ chain quickly: it is a list of things that happened, one after the other.
slides.note_ar: اِقْرَأْ سِلْسِلَةَ «فَـ» بِسُرْعَةٍ: هِيَ أَحْدَاثٌ تَتَتَابَعُ.

rows: The monkey said: I am here.
The tortoise said: Who are you?
The tortoise said: I am patient.
slides.tip: The narrator says “he” and “she”. A character says أَنَا (I) and أَنْتَ (you).
slides.tip_ar: الرَّاوِي يَقُولُ «هُوَ» وَ«هِيَ»، وَالشَّخْصِيَّةُ تَقُولُ «أَنَا» وَ«أَنْتَ».

slides.head_en: Try: which part of the tale is it?
items: بَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَأْكُلُ إِذَا سَقَطَتْ تِينَةٌ
the scene: “and he had settled there”

slides.why: The noun after أَنَّ takes the ـَ ending: أَنَّ قِرْدًا. The correct sentence is: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ مَلِكًا.
slides.why_ar: الِاسْمُ بَعْدَ «أَنَّ» مَنْصُوبٌ: «أَنَّ قِرْدًا». وَالصَّوَابُ: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ مَلِكًا.

slides.head_en: A tale from Kalīla wa-Dimna: the monkey
lines: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا يُقَالُ لَهُ مَاهِرٌ كَانَ مَلِكَ الْقِرَدَةِ، وَكَانَ قَدْ كَبِرَ وَهَرِمَ،
They claimed that there was a monkey called Māhir who was king of the monkeys, and he had grown old and frail;
فَوَثَبَ عَلَيْهِ قِرْدٌ شَابٌّ مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَمْلَكَةِ فَتَغَلَّبَ عَلَيْهِ، وَأَخَذَ مَكَانَهُ،
so a young monkey of the royal house leapt on him, overcame him and took his place.
فَخَرَجَ هَارِبًا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّاحِلِ، فَوَجَدَ شَجَرَةً مِنْ شَجَرِ التِّينِ فَارْتَقَى إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَهَا مَقَامَهُ.
He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.
slides.source: Kalīla wa-Dimna (Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ), "The Monkey and the Tortoise"

lines: زعموا أن قردًا يقال له ماهر كان ملك القردة، وكان قد كبر وهرم،
They claimed that there was a monkey called Māhir who was king of the monkeys, and he had grown old and frail;
فوثب عليه قرد شاب من بيت المملكة فتغلب عليه، وأخذ مكانه،
so a young monkey of the royal house leapt on him, overcame him and took his place.
فخرج هاربًا على وجهه حتى انتهى إلى الساحل، فوجد شجرةً من شجر التين فارتقى إليها وجعلها مقامه.
He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.
slides.source: Kalīla wa-Dimna (Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ), "The Monkey and the Tortoise"

sections.name: A
sections.en: A tale of Kalīla wa-Dimna. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فَخَرَجَ هَارِبًا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّاحِلِ، فَوَجَدَ شَجَرَةً مِنْ شَجَرِ التِّينِ فَارْتَقَى إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَهَا مَقَامَهُ.
He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.

فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَأْكُلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ التِّينِ إِذَا سَقَطَتْ مِنْ يَدِهِ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ، فَسَمِعَ لَهَا صَوْتًا وَإِيقَاعًا، فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ وَيَرْمِي فِي الْمَاءِ، فَأَطْرَبَهُ ذَلِكَ.
One day, while he was eating of those figs, a fig fell from his hand into the water; he heard a sound and a splash from it, so he went on eating and throwing into the water, and that delighted him.
فَهَذَا مَثَلُ الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَطْلُبُ الْحَاجَةَ فَإِذَا ظَفِرَ بِهَا أَضَاعَهَا.
This is the likeness of the man who seeks a need and, when he gains it, loses it. (The moral, as the tale ends on the next page.)
sections.source: Kalīla wa-Dimna (Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ), "The Monkey and the Tortoise"

items.model: He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.

items.en: Who is “he” in line 1? Look back at the slides.
items.ar_q: مَنْ هُوَ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى الشَّرَائِحِ.
items.model: Māhir, the old king of the monkeys, who was overcome by a young monkey of the royal house.

items.en: What did he do after he found the tree?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بَعْدَ أَنْ وَجَدَ الشَّجَرَةَ؟
options: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا
He climbed it and made it his home.
items.answer: He climbed it and made it his home.
items.model: He climbed it and made it his home.
One day, while he was eating of those figs, a fig fell from his hand into the water; he heard a sound and a splash from it, so he went on eating and throwing into the water, and that delighted him.

items.en: What is the turn of the tale, and which word brings it?
items.ar_q: مَا مُفَاجَأَةُ الْحِكَايَةِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَأْتِي بِهَا؟
options: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا
He climbed it and made it his home.
items.answer: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا
items.model: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا (“suddenly”).

items.en: True or false: the monkey was angry at the splash.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: غَضِبَ الْقِرْدُ مِنَ الصَّوْتِ.
items.model: False. The sound delighted him (فَأَطْرَبَهُ ذَلِكَ).

items.en: Put in order: (a) he reaches the shore (b) a fig falls into the water (c) he climbs the tree.
items.ar_q: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) يَصِلُ إِلَى السَّاحِلِ (ب) تَسْقُطُ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ (ج) يَصْعَدُ الشَّجَرَةَ.
options: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا
He climbed it and made it his home.

items.model: So this is the likeness of the man who seeks a need and, when he gains it, loses it.

items.en: Find the word that means “need”. Which word of line 3 shows that the man loses it?
items.ar_q: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى مَا يَطْلُبُهُ الرَّجُلُ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الضَّيَاعِ؟
items.model: الْحَاجَةَ is “the need”. أَضَاعَهَا (“lost it”) shows the loss.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A fable (a tale with animal characters and a moral) from Kalīla wa-Dimna by Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ.

items.en: ★ Line 2 chains فَسَمِعَ، فَجَعَلَ، فَأَطْرَبَهُ. What does the chain do to the pace of the story?
items.ar_q: ★ سِلْسِلَةُ «فَـ» فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ بِسُرْعَةِ الْحِكَايَةِ؟
items.model: It makes the events follow one another at once, like a list: heard, went on, delighted.

items.en: ★ How does the monkey’s throwing of the figs show the moral of line 3?
items.ar_q: ★ كَيْفَ يُبَيِّنُ رَمْيُ الْقِرْدِ لِلتِّينِ الْعِبْرَةَ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
items.model: He has a tree of figs (what he needed) and wastes them for a moment’s pleasure: he gains the need and loses it.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A tale told at the rawḥa. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً كَانَتْ تَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي.
They claimed that a tortoise used to live near the wadi.
وَكَانَ قِرْدٌ شَابٌّ قَدْ سَكَنَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ تِينٍ هُنَاكَ.
And a young monkey had settled on a fig tree there.
وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ يَأْكُلُ مِنَ التِّينِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَيَرْمِي بَعْضَهُ فِي الْمَاءِ.
The monkey used to eat of the figs every day and throw some of them into the water.
وَكَانَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَجْمَعُ التِّينَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَتَحْمِلُهُ إِلَى بَيْتِهَا.
And the tortoise used to gather the figs from the water and carry them to her house.
فَسَأَلَ الْقِرْدُ: لِمَاذَا تَجْمَعِينَ التِّينَ؟ فَقَالَتْ: لِأَنَّ التِّينَ لَا يَكُونُ كَثِيرًا دَائِمًا.
So the monkey asked: Why do you gather the figs? She said: Because figs are not always plentiful.
But the monkey did not listen to her words.
فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ إِذَا الشَّجَرَةُ لَيْسَ فِيهَا تِينٌ.
One day, while he was looking at the tree, suddenly the tree had no figs in it.
فَنَزَلَ حَزِينًا إِلَى الْوَادِي وَطَلَبَ التِّينَ مِنَ السُّلَحْفَاةِ.
So he came down sadly to the wadi and asked the tortoise for figs.
فَقَالَتْ: خُذْ هَذَا التِّينَ وَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ. فَقَالَ الْقِرْدُ: فَهِمْتُ الْآنَ.
She said: Take these figs and thank Allah. The monkey said: Now I understand.
فَهَذِهِ عِبْرَةٌ: مَنْ جَمَعَ وَجَدَ، وَمَنْ رَمَى لَمْ يَجِدْ.
So this is the lesson: whoever gathers finds, and whoever throws away does not find.

items.en: Who are the two animals, and where do they live?
items.model: A tortoise, who lives near the wadi, and a young monkey, who lives on a fig tree there.

items.en: What did the monkey do with the figs every day?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا كَانَ يَفْعَلُ الْقِرْدُ بِالتِّينِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
items.model: He ate of them and threw some of them into the water.

items.en: What did the tortoise do with the figs?
items.model: She gathered them from the water and carried them to her house.

items.en: Translate line 5 (the question and the answer).
items.model: So the monkey asked: Why do you gather the figs? She said: Because figs are not always plentiful.

items.en: True or false: the monkey listened to the tortoise.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: سَمِعَ الْقِرْدُ كَلَامَ السُّلَحْفَاةِ.
items.model: False. لَمْ يَسْمَعْ = he did not listen.
items.note: لَمْ يَسْمَعْ = he did not listen.

items.en: Find the turn: which two words (بَيْنَمَا … إِذَا) frame it? What was the surprise?
items.ar_q: جِدِ الْمُفَاجَأَةَ: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُحِيطَانِ بِهَا؟ وَمَا هِيَ؟
items.model: فَبَيْنَمَا … إِذَا. The surprise: the tree had no figs left.

items.en: How did the tortoise treat the monkey when he came down sadly?
items.ar_q: كَيْفَ عَامَلَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ الْقِرْدَ حِينَ نَزَلَ حَزِينًا؟
items.model: She gave him figs (خُذْ هَذَا التِّينَ) and told him to thank Allah.

items.en: Who says “Now I understand”, and what has he understood?
items.model: The monkey. He has understood the tortoise’s words: do not waste what you have.

items.en: Translate the last line: the moral.
items.model: So this is the lesson: whoever gathers finds, and whoever throws away does not find.

items.en: Which word tells you that a moral follows? Which word opens the tale?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْعِبْرَةِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَفْتَحُ الْحِكَايَةَ؟
items.model: عِبْرَةٌ (“lesson”) tells you the moral follows. زَعَمُوا أَنَّ opens the tale.

items.en: ★ Lines 3 and 4 use كَانَ + present (كَانَ يَأْكُلُ … وَكَانَتْ تَجْمَعُ), but the later events use plain past verbs after فَـ. Why?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَسْتَعْمِلُ السَّطْرَانِ ٣ وَ٤ «كَانَ + الْمُضَارِعَ»؟ وَلِمَاذَا تَسْتَعْمِلُ الْأَحْدَاثُ بَعْدَهُمَا الْمَاضِيَ؟
items.model: The كَانَ + present lines describe what the animals used to do every day (the scene). The plain past verbs tell what happened on one day (the plot).

items.en: ★ Compare this tale with the monkey of Kalīla wa-Dimna (Exercise A). What do the two monkeys share?
items.ar_q: ★ قَارِنْ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْحِكَايَةِ وَقِرْدِ كَلِيلَةَ وَدِمْنَةَ. مَاذَا يَشْتَرِكُ فِيهِ الْقِرْدَانِ؟
items.model: Each monkey has plenty of figs and wastes them by throwing them away; each tale ends by telling us not to lose what we have gained.

قَدْ goes with a past verb: كَانَ قَدْ أَكَلَ (“he had eaten”). For a habit use كَانَ يَأْكُلُ.
The doer is feminine, so the verb must be feminine too: تَجْمَعُ.

lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.
وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.
So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.
وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا.
The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision.
وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.
سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الرَّجُلُ الرُّطَبَ فِي السُّوقِ؟
Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market?
The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَتْنِ عَنِ الْإِعْرَابِ: وَأَقْسَامُهُ أَرْبَعَةٌ: رَفْعٌ وَنَصْبٌ وَخَفْضٌ وَجَزْمٌ.
The boy read in the matn about iʿrāb: Its kinds are four: rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ and jazm.
وَعَرَفَ الْوَلَدُ أَنَّ الضَّمَّةَ عَلَامَةُ الرَّفْعِ.
And the boy knew that the ḍamma is the sign of rafʿ.
اِسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى تَسْجِيلِ دَرْسٍ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy listened to a recording of a lesson by the Habib.
And the boy understood all the words of the Habib.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْأَخْبَارِ: نَزَلَتِ الْأَمْطَارُ فِي الْوَادِي.
The boy heard on the news: Rain fell in the wadi.
And it was announced that the rain was very heavy.
The boy wrote a letter home.
وَكَتَبَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا تَحِيَّةً لِأُمِّهِ وَفِي آخِرِهَا تَوْقِيعَهُ.
He wrote at its beginning a greeting to his mother, and at its end his signature.
خَلَطَتْ فَاطِمَةُ الدَّقِيقَ وَالْمَاءَ وَالْمِلْحَ فِي إِنَاءٍ كَبِيرٍ.
Fatima mixed the flour, the water and the salt in a large bowl.
ثُمَّ عَجَنَتِ الْعَجِينَ وَخَبَزَتْهُ فِي الْفُرْنِ.
Then she kneaded the dough and baked it in the oven.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى السُّوقِ قَبْلَ صَلَاةِ الْجُمُعَةِ.
The boy went to the market before the Friday prayer.
سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ: مَا سِعْرُ الْكِيلُو؟ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: مِائَةُ رِيَالٍ، وَهُوَ أَجْوَدُ تَمْرٍ.
The boy asked: What is the price of a kilo? The man said: One hundred riyals, and it is the finest dates.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ حِكَايَةً: يُحْكَى أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ صَدِيقَ سُلَحْفَاةٍ.
In the rawḥa the boy read a tale: It is told that a monkey was a friend of a tortoise.
And at its end is a lesson for every friend.
